title: WAN Upload Saturation During Backup Window
dataSources: UniFi controller events (`unifi:event`), Pi-hole query log (`pihole:query`), AdGuard Home (`adguard:query`), speedtest-cli results (`speedtest:result`), router/firewall syslog, ISP uptime probes (`uptime:probe`).
app: UniFi / router syslog, Pi-hole/AdGuard, and scheduled speedtests via HEC scripted inputs and the Universal Forwarder.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=unifi:event
| eval hour=strftime(_time,"%H")
| where hour>=1 AND hour<=5
| bin _time span=1d
| stats max(tx_mbps) as peak_upload by wan_interface _time
| where peak_upload>80
| sort - peak_upload
description: Looks for overnight backup windows where upload demand gets close to saturating the WAN link and potentially starves everything else.
value: Home backups, camera uploads, and cloud sync jobs all compete for the same narrow upstream; seeing the worst spikes helps you schedule them sanely.
implementation: Forward WAN interface throughput from UniFi or router logs; review the overnight peak-upload window and stagger the chattiest jobs.
visualization: Daily chart of overnight peak upload throughput by WAN interface.
grandmaExplanation: It compares when overnight backups or cloud syncs are almost maxing out your home's upload speed.
